itinerary.labelHtml:
The Itinerary

Day by day

Swipe each carousel for photos. Every stop carries its cost, a 💰 money-saving tip, an ✨ splurge, picky-kid restaurants, backup / if-time ideas, blog links, and a map — tap “Open in Google Maps” to navigate. Each day also shows an estimated per-day cost — food + activities only (excludes lodging, flights, and the rental car).

days.heading: Depart Pittsburgh after work

facts.label: PTO
facts.valueHtml: No PTO if after-work departure works

days.note: Price Dubrovnik and Tirana, but Dubrovnik is the route-friendly arrival. Tirana only wins if fare savings are big enough to justify the long northbound drive.

days.heading: Land, pick up car, drive to Mostar
days.note: Keep this day simple: border, check-in, dinner, and first bridge views. Do not schedule Kravica after an overnight flight.

spots.name: Mostar Old Town + Stari Most
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · MostarIG · Stari MostFlickr
spots.cost: Old Bridge and bazaar are free. Koski Mehmed Pasha Mosque/minaret is paid; recent reports conflict around EUR7-EUR15, so ask at the door.
spots.climate: July: hot, often upper 80s to low 90s F daytime / upper 60s F nights. Neretva swimming is cold and local-condition dependent.
spots.saveHtml: Save Stay walkable and skip paid viewpoints; the bridge, bazaar, riverbanks, and sunset angles are free.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Pay for the mosque/minaret viewpoint if open; budget roughly EUR30-EUR60 family depending the current tariff.
spots.restoHtml:
• Restaurant-Pizzeria Megi — pizza, pasta, lasagna, steaks, cakes; plain pizza/pasta works
  • Nide Veze — pizza, sandwiches, pancakes, waffles; Margherita pizza is the easy order
  • Restoran Vodopad Kravice — at the falls; burger/fries, chicken, and pizza-style options reported
spots.altboxHtml:
• Pocitelj ↩ — a compact Ottoman stone village if Mostar feels crowded.
  • Koski Mehmed Pasha Mosque viewpoint ↗ — quick terrace/minaret view over Stari Most if you want the bridge payoff without another long walk.
  • Blagaj Buna canals ↗ — riverside restaurants and ducks by the spring if the Tekke interior is not a priority.

days.heading: Blagaj cliff spring and Kravica swim
days.note: This is the Herzegovina day that justifies Mostar as a base: cliff monastery in the morning, waterfall swimming later when heat peaks.

spots.name: Blagaj Tekke + Buna Spring
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Blagaj TekkeIG · Buna SpringFlickr
spots.cost: Outside river views are free. Tekke interior is unconfirmed but recent sources report about 10 KM / EUR5 per person.
spots.climate: Hot afternoons; go morning or late day. The cliff spring area feels cooler than Mostar old town.
spots.saveHtml: Save See the Tekke from the riverside restaurants and bridge for free if the kids are not interested in the interior.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Do a riverside lunch with the cliff view; expect a higher tourist-location bill than Mostar.
spots.restoHtml:
• Restaurant-Pizzeria Megi — pizza, pasta, lasagna, steaks, cakes; plain pizza/pasta works
  • Nide Veze — pizza, sandwiches, pancakes, waffles; Margherita pizza is the easy order
  • Restoran Vodopad Kravice — at the falls; burger/fries, chicken, and pizza-style options reported
spots.altboxHtml:
• Dervish House viewpoint only ↩ — keeps the visual payoff without committing to a full interior visit.
  • Blagaj Buna canals ↗ — riverside restaurants and ducks by the spring if the Tekke interior is not a priority.
  • Mogorjelo Roman villa ↗ — small ruins stop near Capljina when culture wins over waterfall crowds.

spots.name: Kravica Waterfalls
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Kravica WaterfallsFlickr
spots.cost: Official 2026 pricing: 20 KM adult, 10 KM ages 7-18, under 7 free; parking 3 KM/hour or 6 KM/day. Family estimate: 60 KM plus parking.
spots.climate: Water is cool, roughly high 60s F to low 70s F in summer, but swimmable in hot weather.
spots.saveHtml: Save Bring towels, water shoes, and snacks so the falls are a half-day swim/picnic instead of a restaurant day.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Use the on-site restaurant and stay through late afternoon light; budget about 80-120 KM for an easy meal.
spots.restoHtml:
• Restaurant-Pizzeria Megi — pizza, pasta, lasagna, steaks, cakes; plain pizza/pasta works
  • Nide Veze — pizza, sandwiches, pancakes, waffles; Margherita pizza is the easy order
  • Restoran Vodopad Kravice — at the falls; burger/fries, chicken, and pizza-style options reported
spots.altboxHtml:
• Buna canals near Blagaj ↩ — less of a swim spectacle, but easier if Kravica crowds look rough.
  • Mogorjelo Roman villa ↗ — small ruins stop near Capljina when culture wins over waterfall crowds.
  • Kravica picnic edge ↗ — quieter riverside pause if the main waterfall viewing area is packed.

days.heading: Drive to the Bay of Kotor
days.note: Route via Trebinje/Sitnica rather than backtracking through Dubrovnik unless live border conditions make the coast better.

spots.name: Kotor Old Town + City Walls
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · KotorFlickr
spots.cost: City walls/San Giovanni fortress currently reported at EUR15 per person, under 12 free; family estimate about EUR45.
spots.climate: July: around low-to-mid 80s F days / upper 60s to low 70s nights. Bay water averages about 77-79 F.
spots.saveHtml: Save Climb early, carry water, and skip paid boat tours on this day; old-town wandering is free.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Private or small-group bay boat after the climb; expect EUR100+ family depending duration.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzeria Pronto — wood-fired pizza in Kotor Old Town; order Margherita
  • BBQ Tanjga — casual grilled meats; chicken and fries are the picky-kid backup
  • Babaluu — Budva kids menu with chicken fingers, burgers, fries, pasta, and pizza
spots.altboxHtml:
• Ladder of Kotor lower viewpoint ↩ — similar views if the full fortress climb is too hot.
  • Lovcen viewpoint ↗ — big mountain scenery if you want views more than a beach day and can handle the drive.
  • Dobrota waterfront ↗ — flat bay walk and swim access when Kotor Old Town is hot and crowded.

days.note: This can become too much if traffic is bad. If everyone wants water more than towns, skip Budva and swim near the bay.

spots.cost: Perast waterfront is free. Boat to Our Lady of the Rocks commonly runs EUR5-EUR10 pp return; church/museum often EUR2-EUR3 pp.
spots.climate: Warm bay day; water is usually comfortable, shade is limited along the waterfront.
spots.saveHtml: Save Drive or taxi to Perast and use the short local boat instead of a longer Kotor speedboat tour.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Take a 2-hour bay boat from Kotor if parking stress matters more than price; plan EUR25+ per person.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzeria Pronto — wood-fired pizza in Kotor Old Town; order Margherita
  • BBQ Tanjga — casual grilled meats; chicken and fries are the picky-kid backup
  • Babaluu — Budva kids menu with chicken fingers, burgers, fries, pasta, and pizza
spots.altboxHtml:
• Dobrota waterfront swim ↩ — simpler, cheaper, and close to Kotor if the family wants downtime.
  • Porto Montenegro ↗ — polished marina, food, and easy strolling if the family wants low-friction downtime.
  • Lustica coves ↗ — more cove time and less old-town traffic than Budva or Sveti Stefan.

spots.cost: Budva old town and Sveti Stefan viewpoints are free; parking is variable, often around EUR1-EUR4/hour in busy areas.
spots.climate: Hot coastal afternoon; build in a swim and avoid trying to sightsee all day.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use Sveti Stefan as a viewpoint/photo stop instead of paying for resort-adjacent extras.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Beach-club loungers near Budva/Sveti Stefan can turn the day easy; confirm the set price before sitting.
spots.restoHtml:

days.heading: Long drive to Ksamil
days.note: Leave early and treat the day as logistics. If the drive looks like too much, insert Gjirokaster and cut one Corfu night.

spots.name: Ksamil Beaches + Islands
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · KsamilFlickr
spots.cost: SunEasy lists Ksamil beach sets around 1,000-1,700 ALL/day for some clubs; central/popular spots can run 2,000-4,000 ALL.
spots.climate: July: hot beach weather, often mid-to-upper 80s F daytime; sea averages about 76-78 F, usually the warmest water of the trip.
spots.saveHtml: Save Pick an off-center beach or late-afternoon set; central first-row loungers are where prices jump.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Rent kayaks/pedal boat or take a short island boat hop; confirm the price before boarding.
spots.restoHtml:
• Limani Sarande — Margherita pizza, fries, chicken fillet, penne chicken, club sandwich
  • Family Restaurant Ksamil — Bolognese, pasta alla crema, schnitzel, grilled chicken fillet
  • L'arte Della Pizza Ksamil — pizza, pasta, burgers, and kid-friendly basics
spots.altboxHtml:
• Pulbardha Beach ↩ — a prettier escape if central Ksamil feels packed.
  • Saranda promenade ↗ — low-effort evening walk, snacks, and water views without committing to a day trip.
  • Gjirokaster old town ↗ — stone-roofed UNESCO town if you want culture instead of another beach stop.

facts.label: Afternoon

days.note: Butrint and Blue Eye are both worthwhile, but doing both plus a beach is a lot. If the kids need water, keep Blue Eye as the optional swap.

spots.name: Butrint National Park
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · ButrintFlickr
spots.cost: Official pricing: 1,000 ALL adult, 500 ALL ages 12-18, under 12 free. Family estimate: 2,500 ALL.
spots.climate: Warm and exposed; go early, then use the afternoon for beach recovery.
spots.saveHtml: Save Drive yourselves from Ksamil, arrive early, and skip guided add-ons unless the kids want ruins context.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Hire a guide or combine with a relaxed seafood lunch on the Vivari Channel.
spots.restoHtml:

  • Family Restaurant Ksamil — Bolognese, pasta alla crema, schnitzel, grilled chicken fillet
  • L'arte Della Pizza Ksamil — pizza, pasta, burgers, and kid-friendly basics
spots.altboxHtml:

spots.name: The Blue Eye
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Blue EyeFlickr
spots.cost: Recent 2026 visit report: 50 ALL/person entry, 300 ALL parking up to 3 hours, tourist train 300 ALL one-way or 600 ALL round trip.
spots.climate: Cool spring water, hot walk. Swimming is restricted at the spring itself; treat it as a nature stop, not a full swim day.
spots.saveHtml: Save Walk the 20-30 minutes instead of taking the train if the heat is manageable.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Use the train both ways with kids if the day is hot; family train round trip can be about 2,400 ALL.
spots.restoHtml:

days.heading: Return car, ferry Saranda to Corfu
days.note: Build in passport-control time and remember Greece is one hour ahead. Keep Corfu arrival to check-in, Old Town, and dinner.

spots.name: Corfu Town + Old Fortress
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · CorfuIG · Old FortressFlickr
spots.cost: Official Old Fortress / Byzantine Collection ticket is EUR10; family estimate EUR40 unless child reductions apply at booking.
spots.climate: July: warm to hot, often upper 80s F days; Ionian water is typically upper 70s F.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use the Liston, old lanes, harbor views, and sunset walks as the free half of the day.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Do the Old Fortress plus a nicer last-night dinner in town; budget EUR120-EUR180 family.
spots.restoHtml:
• Old Times Corfu — pizza, linguine carbonara/Bolognese, fries, chicken fillet, gyros
  • Vrachos Paleokastritsa — kids chicken nuggets, hamburger, tomato pasta, fries
  • Pazuzu Glyfada — burger with fries, crispy chicken, spaghetti pomodoro, roasted chicken
spots.altboxHtml:
• Mon Repos park ↩ — a greener, lower-key substitute if fortress heat is too much.
  • Angelokastro ↗ — castle ruins and big views if the family wants a short climb instead of caves.
  • Aqualand Corfu ↗ — straight kid backup when beaches are windy or everyone wants slides.

days.heading: Beach-and-boat day in Paleokastritsa

facts.label: Plan
facts.valueHtml: Coves, caves, or Paradise Beach boat

days.note: This is the reward day: use it for water, not errands. Book boat time only if the sea looks calm.

spots.name: Paleokastritsa Beaches + Caves
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · PaleokastritsaFlickr
spots.cost: Boat pricing varies: general Paradise Beach boats often EUR15-EUR20 pp; operator listings showed tours from EUR55. Beach set pricing varies by cove.
spots.climate: Swim day; coves are clear, and the water should be comfortably warm in July, with limited shade away from the beach umbrellas.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use public beaches and a short water taxi instead of a full private boat.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a longer cave/Paradise Beach boat if the sea is calm; this is one of the trip's best splurge days.
spots.restoHtml:
• Old Times Corfu — pizza, linguine carbonara/Bolognese, fries, chicken fillet, gyros
  • Vrachos Paleokastritsa — kids chicken nuggets, hamburger, tomato pasta, fries
  • Pazuzu Glyfada — burger with fries, crispy chicken, spaghetti pomodoro, roasted chicken
spots.altboxHtml:
• Rovinia Beach ↩ — nearby, beautiful, and often a better crowd tradeoff.
  • Aqualand Corfu ↗ — straight kid backup when beaches are windy or everyone wants slides.
  • Glyfada Beach ↗ — full-service sand day when Porto Timoni logistics feel like too much.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Paradise Beach boat trip ↗Paleokastritsa beach guide ↗

days.heading: Porto Timoni or Glyfada

facts.label: Choice
facts.valueHtml: Hike/boat adventure or easy serviced beach

days.note: Porto Timoni is prettier and harder; Glyfada is easier and more serviced. Choose based on heat and kid patience, then keep the final dinner close to lodging for packing.

spots.name: Porto Timoni or Glyfada Beach
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Porto TimoniIG · GlyfadaFlickr
spots.cost: Porto Timoni has no facilities; Afionas parking is often EUR7-EUR15/day. Boat taxis can run EUR10-EUR20 pp. Glyfada sets often EUR20-EUR40/pair.
spots.climate: Hot beach day; Porto Timoni hike is 30-40 minutes each way with little shade, so morning is better.
spots.saveHtml: Save Choose one beach and pack water/snacks; moving between west-coast beaches burns time and parking money.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Take a boat taxi to avoid the hike if the heat or kid morale is not cooperating.
spots.restoHtml:
• Old Times Corfu — pizza, linguine carbonara/Bolognese, fries, chicken fillet, gyros
  • Vrachos Paleokastritsa — kids chicken nuggets, hamburger, tomato pasta, fries
  • Pazuzu Glyfada — burger with fries, crispy chicken, spaghetti pomodoro, roasted chicken
spots.altboxHtml:
• Glyfada only ↩ — easier infrastructure, fewer hike logistics, still a classic Corfu beach day.
  • Mon Repos park ↗ — green, shaded, lower-key substitute if fortress heat is too much.
  • Rovinia Beach ↗ — beautiful Paleokastritsa-area cove with a better crowd tradeoff.

Plan Health-Check

What to lock, watch, and expect

Research updated July 2026 for a family of 4, with kids treated as roughly 14 and 9 in trip year 2027. The dates now stay inside Jun 6-Aug 15, 2027 and keep the family in Pittsburgh for the full Jun 23-26 blackout.

Book first

Flights and car need quote-level confirmation

Treat the cap-fit version as valid only if flights stay at or below about $4.8k family, the Balkan rental car stays at or below about $2.4k all-in, and lodging lands near the middle of the ranges below.

Critical

The Balkan rental car probably stops in Albania

Do not assume a Croatia rental can enter Bosnia, Montenegro, Albania, and then go to Corfu. Get written cross-border approval and plan to return the car before the Saranda-Corfu ferry.

Long day

Kotor to Ksamil is the hard transfer

Expect 7.5-8 hours before stops and borders. The plan keeps it as one long day to preserve four bases, but Gjirokaster or Shkoder is the pressure-release valve if needed.

Depart after work Thu Jul 1, land Fri Jul 2, use Mon Jul 5 as the observed Independence Day holiday, and return Wed Jul 14. That keeps the trip to about 8 PTO days without touching the Jun 23-26 blackout.

Carry passports, IDP, rental paperwork, green-card/insurance proof, and enough EUR/KM/ALL cash for small tickets, parking, beach sets, and ferry-port friction.

Save money

  • Fly into Dubrovnik if fares are close. It saves 4+ arrival-day driving hours versus Tirana.
  • Use quote gates. Do not green-light this route unless flights are <=$4.8k family, the Balkan car is <=$2.4k all-in, and lodging is not pricing at the top of every range.
  • Stay outside Kotor Old Town. Parking and family apartments are easier in Dobrota/Prcanj.
  • Use one beach per day. Beach-hopping in Ksamil/Corfu turns into duplicate parking and lounger fees.
  • Book the ferry as foot passengers. Dropping the car before Corfu avoids the most complex rental rule.

  • Bay or Paleokastritsa boat time. These are the water splurges most likely to feel worth it.

  • One guided/history add-on. Butrint or Mostar benefits most if the family wants context.

Travel Tips

The stuff nobody tells you

Updated July 2026 for the July 2027 travel window; re-check flight, rental, and ferry rules before paying because those are the unstable pieces.

Book in roughly this order

  1. Open-jaw flights · first, because route choice depends on DBV/TIA pricing
  2. Cross-border rental quote · before lodging is locked
  3. Lodging with parking · immediately after car plan
  4. Saranda-Corfu ferry · once car drop timing is known
  5. Corfu local transport · after lodging location
  6. Boat days · 1-2 weeks out, then weather-check

Documents

Avoid border surprises

  • Passports. Required for every border and the Saranda-Corfu ferry.
  • IDP. Bring one even if some agencies do not ask; it is cheap insurance.
  • Rental paperwork. Carry written country permissions and green-card/insurance proof.

Car Strategy

The make-or-break logistics

  • Get it in writing. Croatia, Bosnia, Montenegro, Albania, one-way drop, and ferry prohibition should all be explicit.
  • Photograph the car. Do a full video at pickup and drop-off, including wheels and underside edges.
  • Do not ferry the car. Plan the Balkan car to end before Corfu.

Money

Small cash still matters

  • Currencies. EUR for Montenegro/Greece/ferry, KM for Bosnia, ALL for Albania.
  • Cards. Good at hotels and many restaurants, less reliable for parking, small tickets, beach sets.
  • ATMs. Use bank ATMs and decline dynamic currency conversion.

Heat + Swim

Make the day survivable

  • Early starts. Fortress, Butrint, and Porto Timoni are morning activities.
  • Water shoes. Useful for Kravica, bay ladders, Ksamil rocks, and Corfu coves.
  • Shade tax. Lounger sets can be worth it when the alternative is four overheated people.

Food

Picky-kid fail-safes

  • Pizza/pasta anchors. Every base has at least one researched plain-food option.
  • Road snacks. The Kotor-Ksamil day needs grocery snacks before departure.
  • Late dinners. Balkan/Greek summer dinners run later; feed kids something plain before scenic dinners if needed.

Ferry + Time

The Corfu crossing has one hidden trap

  • Time zone. Greece is one hour ahead of Albania in summer.
  • Passport control. Arrive early and do not stack a tight airport plan after the ferry.
  • Tickets. Book online when possible, but keep cash/card flexibility at Saranda port.
